mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return tends to be positive due to lower real borrowing costs encouraging equity investment.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-rate-cut average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by rising consumer confidence (HOUST) predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as stronger labor market momentum supports corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month and HOUST rises by >5% month-over-month
failure_condition: In 20 out of 30 instances where the trigger occurs, the 20-day forward return is negative or flat (cumulative IC < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average signals weakening supply-side constraints, which tends to lift S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 12-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During the 60-day horizon following the trigger, the 20-day forward return is negative in more than 70% of cases (IC < -0.3).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds 2.5% in a month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to anticipated tightening by the Federal Reserve and reduced growth expectations.
failure_condition: Over 10 such inflation surprises, the 20-day forward return is non-negative in more than 80% of cases (IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4% for two consecutive months is associated with a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as market anticipates rate hikes and reduced growth.
failure_condition: During 20 such episodes, the 60-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.25).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly retail sales (not available in the catalog; fallback to proxy: HOUST as a demand proxy) and employment (PAYEMS) both show double-digit increases, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is likely positive due to strong consumer and labor momentum.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >10% and PAYEMS increases by >12% in the same month
failure_condition: Across 15 such double-digit trigger months, the 20-day forward return is negative in more than half (IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining industrial production (INDPRO) for four consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return due to persistent supply-side constraints and reduced corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: During 8 such four-month declines, the 60-day forward return is not negative in more than 40% of cases (IC > -0.15).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in the GDP deflator (not available; use GDPC1 as a demand proxy) exceeds +4% in a month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to expectations of tighter monetary policy and inflationary pressure.
failure_condition: In 12 such months, the 20-day forward return is non-negative in more than 60% of cases (IC > 0.1).
